plan_ref: planning/steward-chamber-2026-08-09/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md :: Wave 9 (C10 - F5 DOM injection law over a REGISTERED slot inventory with a growth rule)
law: Every agent-influenced DOM slot the chamber paints is REGISTERED here, and every registered slot is driven with hostile-string fixtures (markup / script / event-handler / scheme payloads) by tests/test_chamber_dom_law_w9.py, whose injection detector (chamber_dom_law.dom_injection_problems) asserts zero markup executes: strings enter via html-escaped server render slots or textContent/attribute-safe JS setters ONLY, and link targets validate against the fixed internal prefixes below. GROWTH RULE (CI, chamber_dom_law.python_render_problems + js_sink_problems): a NEW render function in a registered module, a CHANGED placeholder count inside an existing render (a new interpolation slot), or a NEW innerHTML-class sink inside the chamber's F5 sentinel region each FAIL the suite by name until this inventory (and the hostile-fixture map keyed off it) is updated; stale rows fail too - a living registry, never a Phase-0 snapshot.
granularity_note: The Python rows sit at RENDER-FUNCTION granularity with a mechanical AST placeholder count per function (every %s/%d/%r interpolation slot in the function's string constants) - the count is how a slot added INSIDE an existing render is caught. The JS rows register the only sanctioned innerHTML-class sinks (each carrying a server-escaped chamber render) inside the sentinel-bounded region of the chamber block; all other chamber JS DOM writes use textContent/setAttribute.

href_law.note: chamber_dom_law.INTERNAL_HREF_PREFIXES is the code-owned source; this record must match it (validated) so the artifact John reviews states the law.
